title: Hidden among the baggage (1 Samuel 10:20–24)
hook: the tall new king hides from his own crowning

segments.voice: Yesterday, the elders asking Samuel for a king, like all the nations. Your line was like all the nations. Did you catch yourself wanting something just because everyone has one? Today, they get their king, if they can find him. Day seven hundred thirty-two.

The whole people is gathered at Mizpah. Samuel is about to name a king, and he does it by lot, so everyone can watch it narrow down. The tribes come near, and the tribe of Benjamin is taken. Then the families of Benjamin, and the family of the Matrites is taken. Then one man: Saul, the son of Kish. Every eye turns to find him. And he isn't there. They look. They call. Nothing. So they do the only thing left, and ask the LORD: has the man come here yet? And the answer comes back: "Behold, he hath hid himself among the baggage."
screen: `BENJAMIN IS TAKEN.` → `SAUL, SON OF KISH.` → `AND HE ISN'T THERE.`

segments.voice: Here is what makes it strange. Saul already knows. Earlier, on the edge of town, Samuel took him aside and anointed him privately, poured oil on his head, and told him God had chosen him. When Saul went home and his uncle asked what Samuel had said, Saul told him about the lost donkeys he'd been chasing, and said nothing about the kingdom. And before any of that, when Samuel first hinted at it, Saul's answer was: am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and isn't my family the least of them all? Gideon said much the same, down in his winepress. So when the lot falls on him in front of everyone, he can hardly be surprised. And he's hiding. Among the gear, the bags and supplies people brought with them. The tallest man in Israel, crouched behind the luggage. The people run and fetch him, and the text says that when he stood among them, he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward. Samuel says: do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There's none like him. And the people shout: long live the king. But not everyone. Some worthless men say, how shall this man save us? They despise him and bring him no gift. And Saul, the text says, held his peace. Readers have heard Saul's hiding in different ways. Some hear humility, a man who didn't want power. Some hear fear, a man who knew how heavy it would be. The text doesn't decide for us. It just shows a man who looked like a king from the outside, crouched where no one could see him.
screen: `ANOINTED IN SECRET, TOLD NO ONE.` · `THE SMALLEST OF THE TRIBES.` · `THE TALLEST MAN, BEHIND THE BAGS.` · `HOW SHALL THIS MAN SAVE US?` · then, large: `HE HATH HID HIMSELF AMONG THE BAGGAGE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: find the role you're hiding from. Settle, and breathe. Is there something you've been asked to do, or know you're meant to do, that you keep ducking? Leading something. Speaking up. Being the grown-up in a hard family moment. Taking the job, or the call, or the responsibility. Find it, and notice where you've been hiding: busyness, jokes, other people's needs, the luggage. Don't force a decision. Just stand up from behind the bags for a moment, in your mind, and let yourself be seen. If you pray, you can ask for the strength to stand. The bell holds the time.
Hidden among the baggage. Where Saul was found when the lot fell on him at Mizpah: the tall new king, already anointed in secret, hiding from his own crowning. Today's word.
Your line: he hid among the baggage. Today, accept one role you fear, even a small one: say yes to the thing you've been ducking. Day seven hundred thirty-two.

howItsDone: Jews read Saul's choosing at Mizpah as part of the Former Prophets; commentators differ on whether his hiding shows humility or fear.

original.note: Hebrew: the gear, the vessels and supplies; where Saul hid in 1 Samuel 10:22.

trapdoor: what you thought: a shy king, hiding at his party.
what it means: a man already anointed in secret, the tallest in Israel, hides from his own crowning, and holds his peace when mocked.
what a scholar hears: before any of it, Saul calls Benjamin the smallest of the tribes, and his family the least.

sources.quoted: Behold, he hath hid himself among the baggage.

notes: Audit: cut 'almost like a smile' (puts a tone on God's answer the text doesn't give) and 'from the inside wanted to disappear' (an inner state the text, which 'doesn't decide', never states).
Verify JPS 1917 wording of 10:22 (the KJV has 'among the stuff'; the index uses 'baggage', the JPS word).
'Long live the king' (10:24) is given without quotation marks; the KJV has 'God save the king'. Confirm the JPS 1917 wording if it is to be quoted.
'The tallest man in Israel' rests on 10:23 (higher than any of the people) and 9:2; confirm the phrasing is fair.
'Worthless men' paraphrases 10:27 (KJV 'children of Belial'); 'held his peace' follows the KJV.
Humility vs. fear readings are attributed to 'readers' and not ranked.
Original: הַכֵּלִים, as in 10:22 ('el-hakelim'); confirm vocalization.

Editor: fixed 'a chapter earlier' (the private anointing is 9:27–10:1, the same chapter as the lot); 'the first king' changed to 'a king' (Judges 9 already made Abimelech king, taught on day 720); 'he's not surprised' softened; added a one-line nod to Gideon's 'least in my father's house' (day 717) so the echo reads as deliberate, not repeated.
